also: don’t say I didn’t warn you

terms.grammar: verb, second conjugation, transitive; with nē or ut + subjunctive
terms.comment: To warn and to advise alike: moneō nē, “I warn you not to”; moneō ut, “I advise you to”.

evidence: Cic. Verr. 1.23: mē, ut magnopere cavērem, praemonēbat (Lewis & Short)

terms.comment: Chiefly “remind” (of what is past, Lewis & Short), but also “warn, urge”.

terms.gloss: warn beforehand, tell someone in advance
evidence: Ter. And. 205: neque tū haud dīcās tibi nōn praedictum: cavē!
Plaut. Aul. 99: atque etiam hoc praedīcō tibi
terms.comment: Not to be confused with praedicō, praedicāre, proclaim. Praedīcō tibi is the comic “I’m warning you”, and nē dīcās tibi nōn praedictum “don’t say you weren’t warned”.

phrases.latin: īnstruit et nātum ‘mediō’que ‘ut līmite currās, Īcare,’ ait ‘moneō, nē, sī dēmissior ībis, unda gravet pennās, sī celsior, ignis adūrat’
phrases.english: he instructs his son too: ‘I warn you, Icarus, keep to the middle course, so that the sea does not weigh down your wings if you go too low, nor the sun scorch them if you go too high’

phrases.latin: nam et monendī amīcī saepe sunt et objūrgandī
phrases.english: for friends must often be warned and scolded

phrases.latin: Inrīdēs? nīl mē fallis. sed dīcō tibi: nē temere faciās; neque tū haud dīcās tibi nōn praedictum: cavē!
phrases.english: Laughing at me? You don’t fool me. But I’m warning you: don’t do anything rash; and don’t say you weren’t told: watch out!

phrases.latin: atque etiam hoc praedīcō tibi, sī Bona Fortūna veniat, nē intrō mīserīs.
phrases.english: and I warn you of this too: if Good Luck herself comes, don’t let her in.

phrases.latin: Tē moneō: sī iterum momorderis, domum ībimus.
phrases.english: I’m warning you: if you bite again, we’re going home.

sources: Lewis & Short: moneo · Lewis & Short: praemoneo · Lewis & Short: admoneo · Lewis & Short: praedico
